8.0.s.en: (1) The superiority of love over knowledge

8.0.0.en: Here our teacher the Apostle Paul speaks about the problem of Christians being exposed to eating the meat of the sacrifices that were offered to idols and then sold in the markets and eaten, whether in homes or in temples. He says to the Corinthians that we all know as believers that in truth there is no idol, and therefore eating what is sacrificed to them and sold in the markets does not affect us at all. But there are among us simple brethren who do not have this knowledge, and this conduct on your part may cause them to stumble. Our feeling that we know and others do not know may lead us to pride and superiority over others, and knowledge alone may harm, but if it is joined to love it becomes beneficial.

8.1.0.en: Here the Apostle Paul carries us to the thought of humility and states a truth that must be clear to everyone: that our knowledge, however much it increases and grows, is nothing but a drop in the sea, as the scholars themselves say; indeed it is incomplete knowledge. And he who is puffed up with his knowledge shows that he is lacking in knowledge, since he is proud although his knowledge is not complete.

8.2.0.en: Love is necessary for the knowledge of God, and the mind alone does not give us true knowledge about God, who knows and delights in the one who loves Him and teaches him by His Holy Spirit.

8.2.1.en: Would that we not rely on our knowledge as much as we rely on our prayer to God to illumine our way, lest we be puffed up.

8.3.0.en: As for the permitting or forbidding of what is sacrificed to idols, this depends on the question: "What is an idol?" And the answer is that it is nothing. The wooden, stone or bronze statues have no life and no authority over the affairs of men, and there is no living, true God except God.

8.4.0.en: What the pagans call gods, and they have thousands of them, in heaven such as the sun and the other heavenly bodies, or on earth such as trees and animals, does not affect the faith of Christians. And even if there exist beings superior to man in power and wisdom, such as the angels and the demons, which were called gods in the Old Testament, "For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords" (Deut 10:17), they too are creatures created by God.

8.5.0.en: But to us Christians, unlike the pagans with their many gods and lords, there is one God, almighty, the Father, the origin and source of all creation, and we love Him and live for Him; and we have one Lord, Jesus Christ, the Creator of all things.

8.5.1.en: If our God is the Creator and Ruler of everything in the world, then let our hearts be at ease and not be disturbed by the changes of life and the offenses or threats of others, for our God is able to fight for us. Let us rejoice in His company every day.

8.6.s.en: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

8.6.0.en: There are some Christians of Jewish origin who know that the idol is unclean and yet eat of what was sacrificed to it, and so become defiled, or Christians of Gentile origin who still think that the idol has power beside Christ their God, so when they eat of what was sacrificed to it they too become defiled. These the Apostle calls weak in their spiritual knowledge, that is, they do not know that the idol is worthless, so their eating what was sacrificed to it is counted uncleanness. But those who are perfect in knowledge, who know that the idol is worth nothing, their eating what was sacrificed to idols is counted as eating ordinary meat which God created, so it is clean food for them.

8.7.0.en: But food does not commend us to God, as the pagans believe that eating what is sacrificed to their idols commends them to their gods. We do not increase in our relationship with God if we eat of what was sacrificed to idols, nor do we lack if we do not eat of it, because it is merely ordinary meat and has no relation to our spiritual worship.

8.7.1.en: This saying is not against fasting. Fasting is a training of the will and not an abstaining from foods because of their uncleanness, since we believe that all foods are blessed by God, but we give up meat as a stripping of our material desires so as to be occupied with the worship of God.

8.8.0.en: You have a right, O strong ones, to eat of those sacrifices, but take heed lest this eating of yours become a stumbling block to your weak brethren whose consciences forbid eating of these sacrifices.

8.9.0.en: O strong brother, who are certain that the idol is nothing and that eating what is sacrificed to idols is like eating any other meat: but if a weak brother sees you eating at a feast held in an idol's temple (as was the custom of the people then, who reclined on couches before the table), he may conclude that you do this in honor of the idol, so he ventures to eat also, imitating you, and in his conscience he eats in honor of the idol, which destroys his soul, though Christ died for him.

8.10.0.en: By this conduct, O strong ones, you sin against the weak, because you push them to violate their consciences by eating meat that is unclean in their eyes because it was sacrificed to idols. And so you sin against Christ by causing the weak to stumble.

8.11.0.en: Therefore, although eating what is offered to an idol is not evil for the believer, who realizes that there is no idol, it is counted evil if it is the cause of others' stumbling; hence, if any food causes my brother to fall into sin, I will refrain from eating of it, lest I be the cause of his stumbling. For as a Christian I am responsible not only for myself but for my brethren also.

8.11.1.en: You must be careful in your conduct and actions so that you do not cause those around you to stumble, even if you intend no evil. But have compassion on those around you as Christ has compassion on you, and do not appear in ways that cause others to stumble.

8.11.2.en: The needs of the servant and his flexibility

9.0.s.en: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

9.0.0.en: Some of the Corinthians doubted Paul's apostleship and could therefore reject his teachings. Here the Apostle Paul affirms his apostleship with proofs, and puts forward several questions which are in fact a statement of the truth, that he is an apostle of the Lord Jesus. The aim of the Apostle Paul in his question "Am I not an apostle?" is to affirm that he is an apostle, and he proves this in the rest of verse 1 and in verses 2 and 3. As for his second question, "Am I not free?", he means that since he is a free man, he has the full apostolic rights like the rest of the Apostles, which include taking support from the Church, as will come later. Then the Apostle presents the first proof, which is that he saw the Lord Jesus and received from Him personally his apostolic ministry, and the second proof is their faith, which is the fruit of his preaching work among them.

9.1.0.en: "Others": those who came to Corinth after Paul left it and did not experience his apostleship, and so doubted it.

9.1.1.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. If I am not an apostle to others, yet to you I am an apostle, and your faith in the Lord Jesus is sufficient proof of the truth of my apostleship, and so you yourselves are the guarantee and confirmation of that. The seal is the sufficient guarantee that the goods sent from one party to another are genuine.

9.2.0.en: This is the proof of the truth of my claim, and what I answer in my own defense to those who investigate the truth of my mission.

9.3.0.en: Have we not the right to live at the expense of the churches that we founded and served in, based on the word of Christ: "And into whatsoever house ye enter... in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire" (Lk 10:7)?

9.4.1.en: Have we not the right to go about preaching with a believing sister as a wife, whose support is also from the Church, like the rest of the married Apostles, who went about preaching with their wives accompanying them to serve their husbands and to preach to the women, and likewise "the brethren of the Lord", that is, the sons of His aunt, who are James, Joses, Simon and Judas (Mt 13:55), who also went about preaching with their wives?

9.5.0.en: Or do only I and Barnabas have no right to this, and must we work to provide for our living needs?

9.5.1.en: Know your rights so that you use them for the glory of God. It is not wrong to claim them, but take care not to lose your peace and clash with others, for your right to peace is more important than material rights.

9.6.s.en: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

9.6.0.en: The Apostle Paul affirms the Church's obligation to meet the cost of his living, and gives three examples that illustrate the answer. The first is the soldier: he says that one cannot expect the soldier, while he fights in defense of his country, to support himself; the second is the vinedresser: he says that the vinedresser feeds himself from the produce of his vineyard; and the third example is the shepherd, who lives on the milk of his flock or its price.

9.7.0.en: I do not say this according to my human opinion, but the Law, which is the law of God by the mouth of Moses, establishes that the preacher may live at the expense of the Church, for it is written in the Law not to muzzle the ox as it treads out the grain, to keep it from eating of what it threshes (Deut 25:4). Does God care for oxen more than He cares for man? God's purpose in this commandment is to establish a general principle, "the labourer is worthy of his hire", that is, the benefit of the workers among people. He who plows the ground or threshes the grain has hope of being rewarded for his labor, and the reward for work encourages diligence in it.

9.8.0.en: If we have preached to you the word of God, which is able to lead you to eternal life, it is not much for us to take from you our material needs for this temporal life.

9.9.0.en: The Christians of Corinth were convinced that other teachers than Paul had the right to take support from them, and that it was unjust not to meet Paul's support, though he was the first to teach them the Gospel and open to them the door of faith. But the Apostle Paul tells them that he voluntarily gave up claiming what was his right, and even bore the pains of need and the toil of manual work, lest anyone think that he served the Gospel out of greed for worldly gain.

9.9.1.en: The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

9.10.0.en: Do you not know that the Levites who perform the service of the temple and assist the priests live on the offerings of the people to it, as God commanded: "The tithe of the children of Israel, which they offer as an heave offering unto the Lord, I have given to the Levites to inherit" (Num 18:24-32); and those who offer the sacrifices on it, who are the priests, the sons of Aaron, take a portion of every sacrifice as God appointed (Num 18:8-24).

9.11.0.en: So also, as God ordained concerning the ministers of religion in the Old Testament, the Lord Jesus Christ commanded concerning the ministers of religion in the New Testament that they take their support from the people to whom they preach, and not do material work to provide for their needs (Mt 10:10, Lk 10:7). Therefore the believer must care to provide for the needs of the clergy and the consecrated, that they may be free for their service without distraction.

9.11.1.en: Would that you care to reward everyone who labors in any work to help you, and give him his due in full, not only with money but with appreciation and encouragement; and know that everyone around you, great or small, needs you to express your love to him.

9.12.s.en: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

9.12.0.en: As for me, by my own choice I did not use my right as an apostle to obtain my living expenses, nor do I mean by what I now write to you to obtain this right which I voluntarily refused to enjoy; for I would rather die of poverty and hunger than change the principle which I took upon myself in the service of the Gospel and of which I boast, which is not to burden anyone.

9.13.0.en: Preaching is not the subject of Paul's boasting; rather, preaching without pay is the reason for his boasting, for that which a person is compelled to do cannot be a reason for boasting to him. Paul preached because the Lord Jesus commanded him to, and if he abandoned preaching his conscience would rebuke him and he would be exposed to the wrath of God for resisting the heavenly call.

9.14.0.en: If Paul's preaching were voluntary, he would have a claim to a reward. But if it is of necessity because it is a divine command, then he is a steward entrusted with what he must do for his master, and he is thereby bound to serve his lord without expecting a reward.

9.15.0.en: The Apostle asks: What then is my reward, since I received no pay in return for my preaching of the Gospel, and did not use the right which the Gospel gave him as an apostle?

9.15.1.en: The Apostle himself answers this question in the following verses, making clear that his aim is to win everyone for Christ.

9.16.0.en: Although I am free and am not a slave to anyone and no one has authority over me in anything, I have labored in the service of many as though I were a slave to them, in order to guide all to Christ.

9.17.0.en: "Them that are under the law": the Jewish proselytes, that is, the Gentiles who became Jews and held to and submitted to the Law.

9.17.1.en: I agreed with the Jews in their customs and traditions and in their manner of living, in what does not conflict with my Christian doctrine, so that I might win their love and they might believe my teachings and obtain salvation. The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

9.18.0.en: As for the Gentiles, that is, the pagans who do not have a written law like the Jews, I did not follow the law of the Jews, as though I were without law, although I hold to the law of Christ and His commandments, which are more perfect than the law of the Jews; and I dealt with the Gentiles by the natural law, which is the conscience in every person, and which is the voice of God that leads us to faith in Christ and His teachings.

9.19.0.en: "The weak": they are those mentioned earlier in this same epistle. They are believers, but they do not have full knowledge of the teachings of the Gospel, and they were hesitant between the permitted and the forbidden among foods, the keeping of feasts and the other Mosaic teachings of that kind.

9.19.1.en: The Apostle Paul says that he did not rebuke the weak for their doubts, but proceeded gradually with them in teaching with all wisdom and gentleness in order to remove these doubts from their hearts. In sum, he says that he accommodated every group in everything that agreed with its behavior that did not conflict with sound faith, so that he might lead all to Christ.

9.20.0.en: I do all this for the sake of preaching the Gospel, that I may obtain the blessings of the service on earth and then the eternal reward.

9.20.1.en: Would that you feel for those around you and share their thoughts and their lives, to win their hearts. For every person needs someone to share with him, and by that you enjoy strong friendships and find it easy to understand them, indeed you are able to influence them and lead them to life with God.

9.21.1.en: You know from what you see in the public arenas that those who run in the race course each strive to win the prize, but only one wins it. That is, merely running on the course does not make the runner deserve the prize, but persevering in the running until he reaches the goal, and so receives the reward.

9.22.0.en: The athlete in the race course had to eat, drink and sleep by rule, and abstain from rich foods and wine, and devote a large part of his time to training. All that was in order to obtain the prize appointed for the winner of the race, which was a material prize that perishes with time, or even with the perishing of the person. But he who strives spiritually receives the crown of righteousness that does not perish. Consequently the crown that does not perish is worth the effort more than the perishable crown.

9.23.0.en: So you must imitate me, for I strive and run toward a clear goal before me, which is winning souls for Christ, and I am confident of attaining the goal. I do not strive in vain like one who boxes the air and benefits nothing, or like one who boxes his opponent and does not hit him, since his blow lands in the air.

9.24.0.en: I master my bodily desires, which can lead me to laziness and luxury and the other passions that war against the soul; I do not allow my bodily desires to enslave me, but subject them to the leadership of the Spirit who works in me, so that after having preached to many I may not be rejected by God because of my negligence, as He said: "Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" (Phil 2:12).

9.24.1.en: Would that you persevere in your spiritual striving every day, holding fast to your prayers and your readings however busy you are, and examining yourself every day to correct your mistakes, and not surrendering to sin because you have been accustomed to it for a long time or because circumstances encourage you to it; and in the session of confession each month you renew your vigor and continue your striving with zeal.

9.24.2.en: Watchfulness and eating what is sacrificed to idols
